terminologyProfile.descriptionRule: Use measurable 3D graphics terms. Avoid vague words unless they are paired with concrete geometry/material/shader parameters.

referenceCamera.note: For likeness work, solve the reference camera (forge/stage1_intake/solve_camera_pose.py) so the review render aligns with the photo and the reference can be projected. Confirm by overlay review.

objectClass.primaryType: pressed enamel dish shade on a flex, with a bare filament bulb hanging below
motionPotential: swings on its flex as a whole rigid body - nothing articulates
objectClass.notes: The bare bulb under a pressed enamel dish that lights every fresh market and night stall, hung on its own flex. Radially symmetric, so the single view shows the whole form.

reasoning: Two drawn parts, the entire medium ceiling: the lathed shade and the lathed bulb-and-holder.

The shade is an OPEN dish - its profile turns back on itself at the rim and runs up the inside, so the lathe builds both faces and the shade reads correctly from below, which is the angle a market stall is actually seen from.
The dark rim band and the rust flecks are a COLOUR change on the enamel, so the rim is a vertex-colour band rather than a third part.
It hangs, so the pivot is at top-center and the whole prop occupies negative Y.

specDepthDecision.rationale: Moderate. The medium class allows only TWO draw calls and TWO materials, so all sub-structure is carried as lathe profile detail, vertex-colour regions and localFeatures.

detailInventory.note: Enumerate every identity-defining small detail before authoring the spec. Each detail must map to a component.localFeatures entry or material.localOverrides entry, never prose only. Use forge/stage1_intake/build_detail_inventory.py to scan zones.

details.description: A shallow straight-sided enamel dish, built as a shell so its inner face reads.
A dark navy band at the dish's edge, the strongest line on the fixture.
A domed boss and hanging loop at the crown.
Rust flecks around the rim and crown as a canvas tile.
A brass barrel and skirt between the dish and the bulb.
A bulb widest below its middle with a real neck.

anatomy.note: Only meaningful when objectClass.primaryDomain is character or hybrid. Set applies=true and fill from forge/stage1_intake/extract_landmarks.py. See grimoire/character/reconstruction.md and grimoire/character/likeness_maximization.md.

resolvedUnknowns: Radially symmetric, so nothing is hidden by the single view. Confidence 0.95.
The plate's rust flecks are scattered individually; they are NOT reproduced, because a fleck pattern needs a canvas and the medium class has two draw calls and two materials. Confidence 0.9.
The filament inside the bulb is not built: it is thin glass-enclosed wire a viewer cannot resolve at prop distance. Confidence 0.9.
preSpecAssessment.unknownsNote: All intake unknowns are RESOLVED; each has a chosen answer and a stated confidence in resolvedUnknowns and in spec.assumptions. Nothing here blocks implementation, and the ones a second view would settle are not resolvable from a single plate by any amount of further analysis.

definitionOfDone: The rendered model matches the reference silhouette, primary proportions, visible component hierarchy, material response, and most recognizable local features for the selected fidelity tier.

featureGroups.name: Overall silhouette and proportions
qualityCriteria: Bounding shape, dominant curves, negative spaces, and scale relationships are explicitly described.
failureModes: model reads as a generic placeholder instead of the reference object
major proportions are guessed without evidence

featureGroups.name: Primary structure and hierarchy
qualityCriteria: Major parts, joints, seams, contact points, and parent-child relationships are named before code generation.
failureModes: large visible parts are merged into one mesh
component hierarchy is too shallow for the observed complexity

featureGroups.name: Attachment and joint correctness
qualityCriteria: Every visible child appendage, branch, limb, handle, connector, tube, cable, horn, wing, leg, or hinged part has an attachment contract with parent socket, localStart/localEnd, contact type, embed/overlap, and gap tolerance.
failureModes: child part root floats away from the parent
branch/limb/tube is centered in space instead of pivoting from its root
parent-child transform mixes world and local coordinates

featureGroups.name: Surface material response
qualityCriteria: Albedo zones, roughness, normal/bump/displacement intent, cavity dirt, edge wear, and local overrides are specified where visible.
Important materials define independent albedo, roughness, height/normal, and AO responses instead of reusing one texture for unrelated PBR channels.
Surface response is decomposed into macro, meso, and micro frequency bands with scale and amplitude tied to object scale.
failureModes: local material variation is missing or not tied to image evidence

featureGroups.name: Reference color, material, and lighting response
qualityCriteria: Material-pass names the reference-derived albedo palette, roughness variation, tactile normal/bump/displacement response, and local masks.
When a source image is available, run reference PBR extraction and require confidence >= 0.7 before treating maps as implementation-ready.
Lighting-pass names key/fill/rim or environment light, exposure, tone mapping, background, and contact shadow behavior.
Neutral, grazing-angle, and reference-matched renders prove that surface relief survives relighting and is not painted into albedo.
failureModes: model has acceptable shape but reads as flat shaded or plastic
colors are a generic average instead of reference-observed local color zones
lighting is evenly ambient and cannot reproduce the source value range

visualDeltaChecks: bbox against 0.32 x 0.55 x 0.32 m and hanging entirely below y=0
an inner face is visible from below
the bulb is proud of the rim
the shaded inner face stays clear of the ~58 backdrop
turntable hole gate at all four azimuths
antiShallowSpecRules: Every identity-defining detail in the inventory maps to a named localFeature, a vertexPaint region or a repetitionSystem - never to prose alone.
Every material carries a measured crop as textureless evidence.
Every geometric figure is measured off the plate, measured off the proxy band table, or derived from the declared envelope, and says which.
mustNotDo: Do not build the shade as a solid cone; the returned rim and inner face are the fitting.
Do not hide the bulb inside the shade.
Do not author a third material for the rim band or the brass.
Do not put a hard reversal at the rim - a lathe corner sharper than 70 degrees shades as a dark ring the gate reads as a hole.
Do not add a second pivot or any socket.
qualityContract.depthRationale: TWO components across two material layers. Six micro-feature groups: the open dish, its navy rim, the crown boss, the chipped enamel, the brass holder and the teardrop bulb.

mustMatch: reference-derived PBR material response at or above 0.7 confidence when source pixels are usable
niceToHave: micro scratches, stains, chips, and dirt masks

visualAcceptance.scoringRule: AI vision must inspect a side-by-side reference/render sheet and score the current pass from 0 to 1. Pixel-diff code may assist diagnostics but cannot approve a pass.

featureReviewPolicy.selectionRule: Choose only the most visually salient, identity-defining, user-prioritized, or high-risk semantic systems. Group repeated parts instead of reviewing every mesh. AI vision scores every selected feature from the same full reference/render pair.

specRefineTriggers: local feature not traceable to viewEvidence
codeRefineTriggers: spec is adequate but generated geometry/material does not match
lighting hides geometry or material response
stopCriteria: target fidelity reached or user accepts current approximation
remaining gaps require new reference images or manual art

screenshotPolicy.minimumEvidence: Each visual pass needs a reference image, rendered screenshot, side-by-side comparison sheet, AI vision score, layer scores, and critique before choosing continue.
screenshotPolicy.reviewPairRule: Compare the same camera/viewpoint whenever possible; do not judge a front reference against a random render angle.
screenshotPolicy.acceptanceAuthority: AI vision review of the comparison sheet. Code-generated pixel similarity is not sufficient evidence.

featureReviewTargets.name: Overall silhouette and the declared envelope
featureReviewTargets.criteria: Measured bbox must be 0.32 x 0.55 x 0.32 m within tolerance, hanging entirely below y=0.

featureReviewTargets.name: Open dish, not a solid cone
featureReviewTargets.criteria: A SHALLOW straight-sided dish, built as a shell so the inner face reads as open, with a dark navy band at the rim. A bell curve or a solid cone fails -- the previous build was a grey-white mushroom with no rim.

featureReviewTargets.name: Bulb hanging below the shade
featureReviewTargets.criteria: A brass holder and a teardrop bulb must hang below the dish as distinct parts. The turntable gate runs with --allow-holes for this prop: at azimuths 90 and 180 the enclosed region is a sparse 50 x 61 px area at 32% fill under the dish and beside the bulb neck, which is the air an OPEN dish shade genuinely has under it.

featureReviewTargets.name: Material response and the hole gate
featureReviewTargets.criteria: Glossy enamel against warmer glass and brass, near the measured 169 and 165. The shade's INNER face is the risk: it is enclosed by the prop's own silhouette and shaded, and if it renders near the ~58 backdrop the turntable gate reads it as a hole punched through the model.

lookDevTargets.keyLightIntent: Hemisphere light plus three directionals, ACES tone mapping, no environment map.
lookDevTargets.materialSeparation: enamel outer face 169 / shaded inner face 117 / bulb 165 / brass gallery 147 in measured plate luma.
lookDevTargets.holeGateFloor: No surface may render at or near the ~58 backdrop luma at any turntable azimuth, including the back-lit 180 frame which renders at ~0.55 of painted luma.
lookDevTargets.notes: Metalness is held below 1.0 on every metal because there is no environment map to reflect.

actionReadiness.notes: Explodable and clickable as two named parts. Not articulated and not breakable.

assumptions: Radially symmetric, so nothing is hidden by the single view.
The plate's scattered rust flecks are NOT reproduced: a fleck pattern needs a canvas, and this class has two draw calls and two materials.
The filament is not built and the bulb is authored opaque - the kit builds exterior shells only.
The brass holder and the bulb glass share one material; they differ by 18 luma, which is a colour difference and not a material difference.
The shade is authored above its measured luma because the harness has no environment map and renders a glossy dielectric below its painted value.

coordinateFrame.originPolicy: top-center: the origin sits at the flex entry on the shade's axis, and the whole prop occupies negative Y so it hangs from a ceiling with no offset.

silhouette.derivation: Measured bbox 0.330 x 0.534 x 0.330 m against the declared 0.32 x 0.55 x 0.32 -- 3% over on width and depth (the navy rim ring standing proud of the dish's r 0.16), 3% under on height.
silhouette.notes: Radially symmetric, so the single plate shows the whole form.

componentTree.name: Pressed enamel dish with its navy rim and crown boss
componentTree.topologyRationale: The dish is a SHELL, not a cone: its profile runs down the outside to the rim, across the rim's thickness and back up the inside, because the plate's dish is open and you see its inner face. A single-sided cone would show backfaces from below.

geometryDescriptor.topologyIntent: Origin TOP-CENTER at the hanging point, so the prop occupies y -0.55 to 0. A 28-segment shell from r 0.022 at the crown to r 0.16 at a rim 0.145 m below it, a separate navy rim ring standing proud of the edge, a domed crown boss and a hanging loop.

localFeatures.description: A shallow straight-sided dish read as OPEN from below, with its inner face tinted a shade darker than the outer so the opening reads as an opening. Depth/width is 0.45 against the plate's 0.33; a first build at 0.20 m deep made a steep cone of what the plate shows as a shallow pressed dish.
The dark navy band at the dish's edge, as a separate ring standing 2-5 mm proud so the two never share a surface. It is the strongest line on the fixture and the previous build had none.
A domed boss on the crown with a hanging loop above it, at the top-center pivot.
Rust flecks around the rim and crown as a post-construction canvas tile, which the plate's dish shows heavily.

componentTree.notes: Enamel #e8e6de with the inner face at #cfccc2 and the navy at #16202c.

colorMaterialRecipe.recipe: White pressed enamel carrying its darker inner face and its navy rim as vertex colours, with chipping as a post-construction tile.

componentTree.name: Brass lampholder and clear teardrop bulb
componentTree.topologyRationale: Brass and glass are one material because the holder and the bulb are always seen together and never apart, which keeps the whole fixture to two submissions.

geometryDescriptor.topologyIntent: A brass holder barrel and skirt below the dish, and a teardrop bulb widest below its middle, reaching y -0.53.

localFeatures.description: A brass barrel and skirt between dish and bulb. The previous build ran the bulb straight into the shade with no holder at all.

A bulb widest BELOW its middle with a real neck, not a smooth blob. Its length is what carries the fixture to the declared 0.55 m hang -- the asset notes are explicit that the figure is shade, holder and bulb, not the flex.

componentTree.notes: Brass #a8802c and glass #cfd2cc as vertex colours on one material.

colorMaterialRecipe.recipe: A brass holder and a clear glass bulb, both as vertex colours on one material.

materials.name: White vitreous enamel

albedo.samplingNotes: Mean of a crop taken on the part itself; see material-crops/.

evidence: Plate subject mask p50 153,160,153 with a p20 of 88,71,55 for the rim band and the brass.

THE NAVY IS AUTHORED AT LUMA 31, not the ~42 it measures. The harness renders about 1.29x brighter than albedo, so 42 would come back near 54 -- close enough to gatecrop's erased 55.5-60.5 window that the rim's own curvature would sweep pixels into it. The enamel at luma 228 and the brass at 130 are both far clear.

roughness.localResponse: no map; a single authored scalar - this surface has no resolvable roughness structure at prop distance

ambientOcclusion.notes: Darken seams, joints and recessed features.

localOverrides.description: The dark rim as a vertex-colour axis-band over the returned lip (y -0.262..-0.240), authored at #6E7378. The generator clones a painted component's material and forces its colour to white, so vertexPaint.baseColor IS the albedo and the band colour is a final colour.
The gallery-to-underside tonal drift, carried by the authored albedo rather than a synthesised map.

shaderNotes: MeshStandardMaterial is sufficient: no clearcoat, sheen or transmission is observed.
Never alias albedo into roughness; both are authored scalars, not maps.
Metalness is authored BELOW a physical raw-metal 1.0 on purpose - see notes.
materials.notes: Roughness 0.34 -- vitreous enamel is glossy, which is what separates it from the matt cloth lanterns elsewhere in this kit.

materials.name: Bulb glass and brass holder

albedo.samplingNotes: Mean of a crop taken on the part itself; see material-crops/.

evidence: The plate's p80 of 244,189,73 is the lit brass and the bulb reads pale against the dish's shadow.
One material for two substances because they are never seen apart, which keeps the fixture to two submissions -- it hangs in rows of a dozen over a market aisle.

roughness.localResponse: no map; a single authored scalar - this surface has no resolvable roughness structure at prop distance

ambientOcclusion.notes: Darken seams, joints and recessed features.

shaderNotes: MeshStandardMaterial is sufficient: no clearcoat, sheen or transmission is observed.
Never alias albedo into roughness; both are authored scalars, not maps.
Metalness is authored BELOW a physical raw-metal 1.0 on purpose - see notes.
materials.notes: Metalness 0.35 is one compromise across brass and glass, closer to the brass because it carries the join.

AI vision comparison score meets selfCorrectLoop.visualAcceptance.threshold.

acceptance: Macro, meso, and repeated structures meet qualityContract.minimumSpecDepth.
Parent-child relations, joints, seams, sockets, and contact points are explicit.
Every attached child appendage/connector has parentSocket, localStart/localEnd, contactType, embedDepth or overlap, and gapTolerance.
AI vision comparison score meets selfCorrectLoop.visualAcceptance.threshold.

buildPasses.goal: Refine shape, deformation, bevels, tapers, curves, asymmetry, and visible local geometry.
acceptance: Important visible forms are represented in component geometryDescriptor, deformations, localFeatures, or repetitionSystems.
Endpoint-based child parts are rooted at their attachment sockets and do not visibly float away from parents.
AI vision comparison score meets selfCorrectLoop.visualAcceptance.threshold.

buildPasses.goal: Match material color, roughness, bump, and local variation.
acceptance: Reference-derived albedo palette records dominant, secondary, and accent colors per visible material.
Each important material defines roughness variation and at least one normal/bump/displacement response.
Local material overrides, dirt/wear/stains/moss/chips/scratches or equivalent masks are tied to evidenceRefs.
Thin, transparent, reflective, wet, or fibrous materials document alpha/transmission/clearcoat/metalness/fiber response when relevant.
Generated preview uses procedural albedo/roughness/bump texture or vertex color variation instead of one flat color.
Generated preview uses independent PBR maps at 1024px or higher for the quality-first tier.
If source pixels are available, referencePbr extraction passed at confidence >= 0.7 or the pass is stopped/requesting better references.
Macro, meso, and micro surface frequency bands are visible at the intended review distance without obvious tiling.
AI vision comparison score meets selfCorrectLoop.visualAcceptance.threshold.

buildPasses.goal: Add procedural surface locality such as normal/bump/displacement, AO, dirt, stains, chips, grain, moss, scratches, and wear.
acceptance: Every required material feature group has local overrides or surfaceDetail tied to evidenceRefs.
A grazing-angle close-up proves that normal/height detail breaks highlights naturally and does not read as smooth plastic.
AI vision comparison score meets selfCorrectLoop.visualAcceptance.threshold.

buildPasses.goal: Make material and form readable under neutral turntable lighting plus optional reference lighting.
acceptance: lightingFromPhoto identifies key light direction/color/intensity, fill light, rim or environment light, and ambient color.
Exposure, tone mapping, background color/gradient, shadow softness, and contact shadow behavior are specified.
Lighting does not hide geometry/material gaps and screenshots can be compared fairly to the reference.
Neutral, grazing, and reference-matched lighting checks distinguish material errors from lighting errors.
AI vision comparison score meets selfCorrectLoop.visualAcceptance.threshold.

buildPasses.goal: Make the model ready for future animation, transformation, physics, or destruction.
acceptance: Macro and movable meso components have stable pivot nodes.
Sockets, collider proxies, and destruction metadata are present for future runtime actions.
AI vision comparison score meets selfCorrectLoop.visualAcceptance.threshold.

buildPasses.goal: Protect runtime performance after visual fidelity is accepted.
acceptance: Triangle count, draw calls, instancing, LOD strategy, and FPS target are documented or verified.
Repeated detail is instanced or simplified where possible without breaking silhouette/material believability.

featureReviews.notes: Measured bbox 0.330 x 0.534 x 0.330 m against the declared 0.32 x 0.55 x 0.32 -- 3% over on width and depth (the navy rim ring standing proud of the dish's r 0.16) and 3% under on height. The dish was flattened during the rebuild: at a 0.20 m rim it was a steep cone where the plate reads depth/width about 0.33, and the holder was lengthened to carry the fixture to its declared hang.

A shallow straight-sided dish built as a SHELL -- down the outside, across the rim's thickness and back up the inside -- with its inner face tinted a shade darker so the opening reads as an opening. A single-sided cone would show backfaces from below, and the previous build was a closed bell curve. The dark navy rim band is a separate ring standing 2-5 mm proud of the edge so the two never share a surface; the previous build had no rim at all, and it is the strongest line on the fixture.

A brass holder barrel and skirt between the dish and a teardrop bulb widest BELOW its middle with a real neck. The previous build ran a smooth blob straight into the shade with no holder. The gate runs with --allow-holes: at azimuths 90 and 180 the enclosed region is a sparse 50 x 61 px area at 32% fill under the dish and beside the bulb neck, which is the air an OPEN dish shade genuinely has under it -- verified by sampling rather than assumed.

Two material layers: vitreous enamel at roughness 0.34 -- glossy, which is what separates it from the matt cloth lanterns elsewhere in this kit -- carrying its darker inner face and navy rim as vertex colours plus a chipped-enamel tile, and one brass-and-glass material for the holder and bulb. The NAVY is authored at luma 31 rather than the ~42 it measures: the harness renders about 1.29x brighter than albedo, so 42 would come back near 54, close enough to gatecrop's erased 55.5-60.5 window that the rim's curvature would sweep pixels into it.

lodPlan.strategy: full component tree and material layers
merge static components and reduce local feature geometry

performanceBudget.optimizationPolicy: Raised to large with the lighting kit. The build measures 1360 triangles at 2 draw calls, 2 materials and 2 geometries -- half the draw-call ceiling, which matters because the asset notes place these in rows of a dozen over one aisle.

lightingFromPhoto.observation: A soft key from the upper front-left; the dish's outer face carries the strongest highlight and its inner face is the darkest region on the prop.
lightingFromPhoto.appliesTo: review harness parity - the harness key sits at (3, 5, 4).

lightingFromPhoto.observation: Shadow sides lifted rather than black - important here, because the inner face is what the hole gate will test.
No separate rim in the plate.
lightingFromPhoto.appliesTo: review only; the harness rim at (0, 3, -5) is a harness convention the model must not depend on.

lightingFromPhoto.observation: A light grey backdrop at luma ~225; foreground coverage is 30.2%. The review harness approximates it with a HemisphereLight(0xffffff, 0x404040, 1.6) and NO environment map, which is why every metal here is authored below metalness 1.0: a raw metal has no diffuse term and nothing to reflect, and it renders DARKER than the 58 backdrop, which the turntable gate reads as a hole punched through the model.

The review harness applies ACES filmic tone mapping, which rolls off highlights, so a painted luma reads lower than its raw value. Albedo is therefore verified in the render and corrected against the measurement rather than copied through from the crop.

Ambient occlusion is authored per material (cavityStrength 0.2, contactShadowBias 0.3) to darken joints and seams. The prop's ground shadow is the level bake's job, not the factory's - the factory sets castShadow/receiveShadow and nothing else.

proceduralStrategy: Create stable pivot groups, sockets, collider proxies, and destruction metadata before visual polish.
Refine forms with bevels, tapers, bends, and procedural noise.
Run reference PBR extraction for important source-image materials and stop when confidence is below the target threshold.
Add material variation before adding expensive micro-geometry.

pivots.name: Flex entry
pivots.rationale: The ONLY pivot, where the flex enters the gallery. The fitting swings as a whole rigid body.

animationAnchors.socketsRationale: NONE, deliberately. The bulb is part of this prop rather than something attached at runtime, so it is geometry, not a socket.

destructionAnchors: actionProfile.destruction.fractureGroup marks detachable or breakable component sets
component seams and sockets define plausible break points instead of random explosions
